patch.value:
## The seam

pm-klxax7 states it directly: "An environment needs a bounded observation whose token cost is declared before the call, so a training run can budget. That is the same requirement as pm-5t33or's contract-declared output budgets, viewed from the environment side, and the two should resolve to one mechanism rather than two."

This item is that resolution. It does not add a second budget system; it establishes that the environment-side requirement is satisfiable by the command-side contract, and fixes the one property the command side does not yet provide: a cost that is knowable *before* the call rather than measurable after it.

## Why before-the-call is the whole requirement

A command budget is an egress ceiling. It guarantees the payload will not exceed N tokens, which is what an interactive agent needs — it never wants to be surprised.

A training run needs the opposite guarantee at a different time. It plans a run of ten thousand episodes against a context window, and it must know the observation cost *while planning*, not while stepping. A ceiling of 4,000 tokens on a call that typically returns 300 is a correct ceiling and a useless plan: budgeting against it overprovisions by an order of magnitude, and budgeting against the typical case has no guarantee at all.

So the observation contract needs both numbers, and it needs them queryable without performing the observation: the declared ceiling, and a calibrated expectation for the workspace the environment is actually running against.

## What already exists to build on

The command surface declares `default_max_estimated_tokens` for 55 of 76 canonical commands, readable from `pm contracts --summary` without executing anything. Intent-scoped read projections (pm-cxr0jb) already select fields by declared intent. Self-reported token accounting (pm-t5dt4z) has any command report the cost of its own output. Bounded output dimensions (pm-hb7ug8) collapse the flag spellings that control size. Reproducible workspace instances (pm-rbcvt2, shipped) give seeded, byte-identical construction, which is what makes a calibration measurement meaningful rather than incidental.

The missing piece is the join: nothing composes "this observation, against this workspace, costs this much" into a single declaration an environment can read once and plan against.

## What this item owns

An observation is a named, versioned selection over pm read surfaces — which commands, which intent projections, which bounds — declared as data rather than assembled ad hoc per environment.

Its cost is published in two forms, both readable without performing it: the guaranteed ceiling, derived from the constituent command budgets, and a calibrated expectation measured against the specific workspace, derived from the emitted bytes of recent serves rather than from a bytes-per-token constant. The `budget-feasible-projection-descent` catalog entry on pm-4k6b establishes that the calibration input must be emitted bytes; this consumes that discipline rather than reinventing it.

The observation is stable under workspace growth in a declared way. An environment that runs against a workspace which grows over an episode must be told whether its observation cost is bounded independent of corpus size or grows with it, per observation, because that single property decides whether a long run is plannable at all.

Degradation is declared, not incidental. When the calibrated expectation exceeds the environment's allowance, the observation degrades along a declared ladder and reports which tier it served — the same descent the packer performs, surfaced to the caller instead of hidden inside it.

## Acceptance shape

Against a seeded workspace, the same observation declaration must produce byte-identical output across processes and machines, and its published expectation must match its measured cost within a declared tolerance. Against workspaces at 10k, 100k and 1M items — the fixtures pm-mi2x already ships — the published bound must hold at every scale or the observation must declare itself corpus-dependent. An observation that silently costs more at a million items than it published at ten thousand is the failure this item exists to make impossible.

## Boundaries

Not the command token-budget contract (pm-5t33or), which declares per-command ceilings. This composes them into an observation and adds the pre-call calibrated expectation.

Not attested reads (pm-8bgeye), which certify that an assembly is reproducible and independently verifiable. An observation may be attested; attestation does not tell a planner what it costs.

Not fleet amortization (pm-tch9cs), which shares assemblies across holders. Cost sharing changes who pays, not what is published.
Observation contract: a declared, versioned observation whose guaranteed ceiling and workspace-calibrated expected cost are both readable before the call, so a training run is plannable

Third of the four seams pm-klxax7 owns, and the epic states its resolution rule: this is pm-5t33or's contract-declared budgets viewed from the environment side, and the two must resolve to one mechanism rather than two. A command budget is an egress ceiling, which is what an interactive agent needs. A training run planning ten thousand episodes needs the cost while planning, not while stepping, and a 4,000-token ceiling on a call that typically returns 300 is a correct ceiling and a useless plan. So an observation must publish both numbers without being performed: the guaranteed ceiling derived from constituent command budgets, and a calibrated expectation measured from emitted bytes against the workspace actually in use. Duplicate check: searched observation/budget/bounded-read lineages and read pm-5t33or, pm-cxr0jb, pm-hb7ug8, pm-t5dt4z, pm-8bgeye, pm-tch9cs; none publishes a pre-call calibrated expectation for a named observation.

An observation is a named versioned selection over read surfaces declared as data; its ceiling and calibrated expectation are readable without performing it; calibration input is emitted bytes rather than a bytes-per-token constant; each observation declares whether its cost is corpus-independent or corpus-dependent and the declaration holds at the 10k, 100k and 1M fixtures; degradation follows a declared ladder and the served tier is reported to the caller; the same declaration against a seeded workspace is byte-identical across processes and machines
Make observation cost knowable before the call so long environment runs can be budgeted deterministically
A training or evaluation run plans against published cost instead of overprovisioning against a ceiling or gambling on a typical case
pm-5t33or is in flight; resolving the environment-side requirement into it now avoids a second parallel budget mechanism
